intro: People all over the world belong to religions. Your classmates, neighbors and friends may keep many different holidays. Some may follow no religion at all. In this unit you will learn how to study religion the way a fair scholar does.

First you will learn three parts most religions have: beliefs, practices and communities. You will learn what five symbols mean to the people who use them. Then you will fill a whole year with holidays. You will find out why some move and some stay put.
By the end, you will be able to describe a religion without judging it. You will use words like belief, tradition and sacred. And you will know when to say "Happy Diwali" or "Eid Mubarak."
bigQuestion: How can we learn about the beliefs and holidays of others in a fair and kind way?

timeline.t: Lunar New Year may begin on a new moon in late January or February
Holi fills the streets with color in spring; Lent leads toward Easter
Passover and Easter often fall in spring; Vaisakhi comes on April 13 or 14
Many Buddhists keep Vesak on a full moon in April or May
Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year, comes in September or early October
Yom Kippur comes ten days after Rosh Hashanah
Diwali, the festival of lights, comes in October or November
Many Christians keep Christmas on December 25
Ramadan and the two Eids move about 11 days earlier each year

words.d: an idea a person holds to be true, such as an idea about God or about how to live
something people do again and again as part of their religion
a group of people who share something and gather together
a picture or object that stands for a bigger idea
beliefs and customs handed down from older people to younger people
very special and set apart for holy use
to tell what something is like without saying it is good or bad
a calendar that follows the sun; a year is about 365 days
a calendar that counts months by the moon; a year is about 354 days
to remember an event or honor a person with a special day
the Muslim month of fasting, set by the moon
a Jewish spring holiday that remembers leaving slavery in Egypt

choices: A group that meets on Sunday
test.why: A practice is something people do. Believing is a belief; a cross is a symbol.

test.q: Which symbol belongs to the Sikhs?
test.why: The khanda is the Sikh symbol.

test.q: The Star of David is a symbol of which religion?
test.why: The six-pointed star is a symbol of Judaism.
It tells what many Muslims do without calling it good or bad.

choices: Very special and set apart for holy use
test.why: Sacred means holy and set apart. Handed down describes a tradition.

test.q: A person who is not sure whether God exists may be called what?
test.why: Agnostic means not sure. An atheist does not believe in God.

test.q: Where do Muslims gather to pray?
test.why: The mosque is the Muslim house of worship.

test.q: How many days are in a sun year?
test.why: A solar year is about 365 days; twelve moon months are about 354.

choices: It is set by the first full moon of spring
It follows the Lunar New Year
test.why: In many churches Easter is the first Sunday after the first spring full moon.

test.q: Which holiday is the Jewish New Year?
test.why: Rosh Hashanah means head of the year.

test.q: Which holiday ends the month of fasting?
test.why: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan.

test.q: Which holiday uses bright colored powder?
test.why: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colors.

test.q: Which verse does the class use for Passover?
choices: Exodus 12:14, "this day shall be unto you for a memorial"
Deuteronomy 6:4, "the LORD our God is one LORD"
test.why: Exodus 12:14 tells people to keep the day as a feast.

test.q: What does Vaisakhi remember for Sikhs?
choices: The first words of the Qur'an
Guru Gobind Singh starting the Khalsa in 1699
test.why: Vaisakhi remembers the Khalsa's start in 1699.

test.q: What is true of the three parts of a religion?
choices: They are sun, moon and stars
They are books, flags and songs
They are kings, priests and soldiers
They are beliefs, practices and communities
test.why: Most religions have what people believe, what they do and who they do it with.

write.prompt: Choose two holidays from this unit from two different religions. Using one text from the unit, such as Exodus 12:14, Luke 2:11 or Qur'an 2:185, explain what each holiday remembers, what people do, and why its date moves or stays.
tips: Name the text you use, like "Luke 2:11."
Start with "Many Christians believe" or "Many Muslims believe."
Compare the two holidays; do not say one is better.
Use unit words like lunar, solar and commemorate.
